svg.title: A patient's TPN bag is nearly empty and the replacement bag has not yet arrived from pharmacy. Which action by the nurse is correct?
svg.desc: NEVER ABRUPTLY STOP TPN — STOPPING ALL OF THAT SUGAR AT ONCE CAUSES REBOUND HYPOGLYCEMIA, so a dextrose-containing solution is hung to bridge the gap until the patient's own bag arrives. Hanging another patient's bag is a MED ERROR: every TPN bag is mixed in pharmacy for one specific patient with that patient's name on it, which is also why a second nurse must verify the bag before it is hung. Slowing the infusion to a trickle is not a safe workaround either, because infusing TPN too slowly gives inadequate nutrition and can also drop the blood glucose. The nurse does not stop or pause a TPN infusion on her own unless she is working with the line itself or suspects a clot or migration.
